bodyMarkdown:
## Paramedic Salary QLD: Convert Hourly to Annual Pay

If you are a paramedic in Queensland or considering a role, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential. This guide uses the standard 38-hour week and the latest Fair Work, ABS, and ATO figures to help you estimate your take-home pay, tax, and super.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay is calculated as:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time paramedic salary QLD, we assume 38 hours per week unless your award or agreement states otherwise. For example, if your hourly rate is $35.00:

- Weekly pay = $35.00 × 38 = $1,330.00
- Fortnightly pay = $1,330.00 × 2 = $2,660.00
- Annual gross = $35.00 × 38 × 52 = $69,160.00

This formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for your own calculations.

### Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. However, paramedics are typically covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher rates. The Queensland full-time ordinary time average (all occupations) averaged $2,039.70 per week in May 2026, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. This is an average, not a median for paramedic salary QLD. For your specific job, refer to [pay guides](/blog) or your enterprise agreement.

### Casual Loading and Your Hourly Rate

If you are a casual paramedic, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. When using [the timesheet](/), you enter your base hourly rate and then check the casual loading checkbox to add 25% on top. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading. For example, a base rate of $30.00 becomes $37.50 with loading. This loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave.

### Tax and Medicare for 2026-27

Resident tax rates for 2026-27 are:
- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The 2025-26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed. For a paramedic salary QLD of $80,000 per year, tax would be approximately:
- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($4,020)
- 30% on $35,000 ($10,500)
- Total tax = $14,520
- Medicare levy = $1,600
- Total tax and Medicare = $16,120
- Net annual pay = $63,880

This is an estimate. HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

### Super Guarantee Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For a paramedic salary QLD, if your annual ordinary earnings are $80,000, super is $9,600 per year. The maximum contribution base is $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. For a paramedic salary QLD, your fortnightly gross is weekly pay × 2. Using the $35.00 per hour example, fortnightly gross is $2,660.00. After tax and Medicare, your net fortnightly pay would be around $2,456.00 (based on the annual estimate). This can help you plan your budget.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026-27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
